newsitem.title: UK: Tesco results outshone by sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Tesco results outshone by sales gain.

text.p: Britain's leading supermarket chain Tesco Plc reported an 11 percent jump in interim profits on Tuesday but what pleased the market most was a healthy boost in sales and prospects of more to come.
"There were no surprises in the headline figures but the second-half trading news was pretty well received," one dealer said.
Profit before tax in the six months ending August 10 rose to 321 million pounds ($498 million) from 290 million pounds last year, on a 14 percent rise in gross sales to 6.72 billion pounds.
Tesco paid out an interim dividend of 3.25 pence, up from 3.05 pence previously.

The company said like-for-like sales stores were currently running 7.5 percent ahead of last year after a 7.0 per cent increase in the first half, and chairman Sir Ian MacLaurin said he expected more to come.
"I would expect us to (be above 7.5 percent)," he told Reuters.
Shares touched a high of 307 pence before easing back to be little changed at 302-1/2 pence by 0835 GMT.

MacLaurin said in a statement that Tesco, which has overtaken arch-rival J. Sainsbury Plc in terms of market share and currently holds 14 percent, would continue to develop its business and believed it would be able to maintain its momentum.
"There will be more developments coming," he told Reuters.
But he played down concerns that the company's latest "Unbeatable Value" price campaign, launched earlier this month, might herald a serious price war.
"No I don't think we are (entering a price war)," he said. "Prices are important...but they are only part of the equation," he added.
Tesco's operating margins were down 0.3 percentage points in the first half, he said, and inflation in stores, currently at around three percent, is "going south (down) at the moment."
But MacLaurin said a stronger UK economy combined with other initiatives could help to boost sales volume in the second half.
Tesco's ClubCard Plus payment card, launched in July as a follow-on to its ClubCard loyalty card, has already attracted more customers than targeted for the whole year.
ClubCard has been so successful since its launch over a year ago that Sainsbury was pushed into introducing its own Reward card earlier this year after at first dismissing the schemes.
"Being first with new ideas has helped us to continue to lead the market," the company said.
Tesco intends to open a total of 32 new stores this year and that, together with extensions, should give a total of 718,000 square feet of new space.
It will also continue to consider expansions abroad, but MacLaurin said "at the end of the day, we have to ask whether it benefits shareholders."
Tesco's dividend growth of 6.6 percent reflects the company's aim of slowing the increase to reflect more closely earnings gains.
For the full year, the company said it expected a "satisfactory outcome."
"What pleases us is that it is another good set of results on good figures last year," MacLaurin said. ($1=.6444 Pound)
